title: DuMateBench: Evaluating Autonomous Agents in Complex Real-World Workflows
summary: DuMateBench replaces clean, capability-isolated agent benchmarks with 200 tasks reconstructed from production user sessions, run in Docker containers with insufficient, unstable, and noisy environment conditions. Adopting it costs engineering time to set up the containerized harness, LLM-as-Judge API calls for scoring, and compute for multi-framework, multi-model evaluation runs. It can fail if the benchmark's tasks do not match the reader's actual production workload, if LLM-judge scoring is inconsistent for their domain, or if teams over-optimize framework choices to the benchmark rather than to their own telemetry.
rationale: As an evaluation methodology it requires no training or cluster, and the reader should test whether its perturbation-based evaluation predicts failures in their own agent deployment before relying on it for framework or model selection.
technique: Real-session agent benchmark with environmental perturbations
